Rule_Statement: A BOQ sub-task (a line carrying a Parent Item Code) is priced off its ROOT ancestor, not its immediate parent: child qty = root qty, child rate = root rate x breakdown% / 100. The parent chain is walked to the top with a cycle guard.
Failure_Behaviour: Broken or circular parent chain returns null, so the Amount cell renders blank rather than a guessed number.
Evidence_Quote: "Child: amount = rootQty x (rootRate x breakdown%/100) -- identical to F4 in schema.ts, so what the grid shows is what the server will store."

Rule_Statement: The BOQ total sums ROOT lines only. A weighted sub-task's amount is already contained in its parent's amount, so summing every row flat double-counts the BOQ.
Failure_Behaviour: Non-root rows are filtered out of the total; no error is raised.
Evidence_Quote: "A weighted sub-task's amount is DERIVED from its parent (parent qty x parent rate x breakdown %), so it is already contained in the parent's amount. Summing every row flat double-counts the BOQ. Top-level rows only."

Rule_Statement: A line with a Parent Item Code requires a Breakdown %, and must NOT be asked for Qty/Rate (the backend derives them). A root line requires Qty and Rate.
Failure_Behaviour: Save is disabled and the missing field is named per line; on submit the line is refused by name.
Evidence_Quote: "A sub-line (one carrying a Parent Item Code) needs a Breakdown % instead of Qty/Rate, because the backend DERIVES a child's quantity and rate from its root ancestor"

Rule_Statement: Every BOQ line requires a Description and a Unit. A sub-task may leave Unit blank and inherits its named parent's unit.
Failure_Behaviour: Missing Description/Unit is listed in the line's incomplete message and in the Save button's disabled reason.
Evidence_Quote: "A sub-task may leave Unit blank and inherit its parent's -- the real backend derives a child's quantity/rate from its root, and the unit follows the same chain."

Rule_Statement: A wholly blank line row is ignored on save. A row with ANY content but incomplete fields blocks the entire save; nothing is written, and the offending row is named.
Failure_Behaviour: Returns an error naming the row and the missing fields; no rows submitted.
Evidence_Quote: "Line ${i + 1} is incomplete -- add ${missing.map((f) => LINE_FIELD_LABEL[f]).join(", ")}. Nothing was saved."

Rule_Statement: A submission where every line row is genuinely blank is a legitimate title-only, zero-line BOQ and is never treated as an error.
Failure_Behaviour: Save proceeds with zero line items.
Evidence_Quote: "a submission where every row is genuinely blank is a legitimate title-only, zero-line BOQ -- the real backend explicitly allows this. Never an error."

Rule_Statement: A BOQ requires a Title.
Failure_Behaviour: Save disabled with "Title" named in the reason; field message shown on blur.
Evidence_Quote: "export const TITLE_REQUIRED_MESSAGE = \"Enter a title, e.g. Civil Works - Phase 1\";"

Rule_Statement: A line cannot be its own parent; a Parent Item Code must match an Item Code on another line; a loop of parents is rejected.
Failure_Behaviour: Field-level message under Parent Item Code on blur; the row's Amount cannot be derived.
Evidence_Quote: "messages.push({ field: \"parentItemCode\", text: \"A line cannot be its own parent\" });"

Rule_Statement: Save on the New BOQ screen stays disabled until there is a Title AND at least one complete line (minimum: Description, Qty, Rate). The reason narrows to what the closest line is still missing.
Failure_Behaviour: Button disabled with a stated reason instead of an enabled Save that fails after the click.
Evidence_Quote: "if (touched.length === 0) { parts.push(\"1 line with Description, Qty, Rate\"); }"

Rule_Statement: Version numbering: the original BOQ is stored as version 1 and each revision as parent.version + 1, but the user-facing label is version - 1 ("Rev0", "Rev1"). Never negative.
Failure_Behaviour: Display-only; an unparseable version falls back to Rev0.
Evidence_Quote: "the backend stores the ORIGINAL BOQ as version 1 ... and each revision as parent.version + 1. The customer counts revisions from zero -- the original is \"Rev0\""

Rule_Statement: The "Current" revision of a BOQ lineage is the latest APPROVED revision; when none is approved it is the latest revision of any status.
Failure_Behaviour: One row per lineage is flagged isCurrent; an empty lineage returns null.
Evidence_Quote: "The latest approved revision of one lineage; the latest of any status when none is approved."

Rule_Statement: BOQ revisions are shown grouped by lineage: root first, revisions indented beneath in ascending version order; lineages ordered by root createdAt newest first.
Failure_Behaviour: A row whose ancestor is missing terminates the walk at the last held row rather than being dropped from the list.
Evidence_Quote: "a row is never dropped from the list because its ancestor is missing"

Rule_Statement: BOQ status vocabulary is draft / submitted / approved / superseded.
Failure_Behaviour: An unknown status has no variant mapping.
Evidence_Quote: "draft: \"secondary\", submitted: \"default\", approved: \"outline\", superseded: \"destructive\""

Rule_Statement: Category on a BOQ line is optional. A line without one reads "Uncategorized" in the Work Progress Report and shows a "no category" chip; it never blocks Save. Categories come from the org-editable category table, not a hardcoded list.
Failure_Behaviour: No error; the line saves without a category.
Evidence_Quote: "a line without one reads as \"Uncategorized\" in the WPR's category-wise view and shows a \"no category\" chip rather than blocking Save."

Rule_Statement: Progress may not be recorded against a parent BOQ line. Parent lines stay VISIBLE in the picker but are disabled with the reason "parent - pick a child".
Failure_Behaviour: Option rendered disabled with the reason; it cannot be selected.
Evidence_Quote: "export const PARENT_LINE_REASON = \"parent - pick a child\";"

Rule_Statement: A BOQ create is only reported as success when the response carries a real saved id AND at least as many line items as were submitted; anything less is refused as "nothing has been saved".
Failure_Behaviour: 502 with a message naming how many line items were submitted versus saved; the create dialog shows it instead of a success toast.
Evidence_Quote: "BOQ was not saved correctly: ${requestedLineItems} line item(s) were submitted but only ${savedLineItems} came back saved."

Rule_Statement: The /api/scope list only forwards recognised `include` values (variation, compare), rebuilt from a closed set rather than passed through.
Failure_Behaviour: Unrecognised values are silently dropped from the upstream URL.
Evidence_Quote: "Only RECOGNISED values are forwarded, rebuilt from a closed set rather than passed through, so this proxy can never put an arbitrary string into the upstream URL."

Rule_Statement: A line's Budget = line amount x budgetPercentage / 100. The budgetPercentage column defaults to 25, so an untouched line reads 25%.
Failure_Behaviour: Recomputed client-side after an inline edit from the server's returned value.
Evidence_Quote: "/** amount x budgetPercentage / 100, rounded once by the backend. */ budget: number;"

Rule_Statement: Budget percent must be a number between 0 and 100.
Failure_Behaviour: Field message before save ("Budget percent must be between 0 and 100"); the backend refuses out-of-range with a 400.
Evidence_Quote: "The backend refuses anything outside 0-100 with a 400; saying so at the field is the difference between a correction and a failed save."

Rule_Statement: A vendor amount must be a number and cannot be negative. An empty value clears the quote (null), which is legitimate.
Failure_Behaviour: Inline field error "Vendor amount cannot be negative"; empty passes and clears.
Evidence_Quote: "if (value < 0) return \"Vendor amount cannot be negative\";"

Rule_Statement: A line's Actual (a.k.a. Committed) cost = vendorAmount + materialAmount + manpowerAmount. It is null, never 0, while none of the three has been entered.
Failure_Behaviour: Renders an en dash rather than a zero, so "nothing costed" stays distinguishable from "costed at zero".
Evidence_Quote: "null (not 0) when none of the three has been entered -- \"nothing has been costed yet\" is a real state and must stay distinguishable from \"costed at zero\"."

Rule_Statement: Variance = Budget minus Actual. A NEGATIVE variance means the line has spent more than its budget (over). Variance is null while nothing has been costed.
Failure_Behaviour: Over-budget lines counted via variance < 0; a null variance is excluded from the count and from the chart.
Evidence_Quote: "Budget MINUS Actual, so a NEGATIVE number means the line has spent more than it was given and the cell reads \"over\"."

Rule_Statement: Only ROOT lines (parentLineItemId null) contribute to any category subtotal or the Grand Total; weighted children are listed for the QS but never counted.
Failure_Behaviour: Child rows are skipped in the subtotal loop.
Evidence_Quote: "if (line.parentLineItemId) continue; // a weighted child is a share of its parent, never money of its own"

Rule_Statement: Subtotal rounding happens ONCE, at the end of each subtotal, over raw values, so the Grand Total reconciles exactly to a raw SQL sum.
Failure_Behaviour: No error; prevents fractional drift against the backend report.
Evidence_Quote: "Rounding happens ONCE, at the end of each subtotal, over raw values -- the same single-rounding rule compliance-tracker's own boqBudgetVarianceReport uses"

Rule_Statement: A line with no category is grouped under "Uncategorized", which is always ordered LAST; a blank cell is never shown for a category.
Failure_Behaviour: Sort forces the label to the end of the group order.
Evidence_Quote: "Uncategorized last: it is a gap to close, not a category of work, and a reader scanning trades should not hit it in the middle of the list."

Rule_Statement: The Budget screen's Grand Total must tie to the BOQ's own total to within 0.01; a larger difference is a real disagreement and raises a banner.
Failure_Behaviour: grandTotalTies returns false, which the screen surfaces as a banner.
Evidence_Quote: "return Math.abs(grandTotalAmount - boqTotalValue) < 0.01;"

Rule_Statement: After an inline budget edit, the row is refreshed from the SERVER's response value, never from the string the user typed, and both Budget and Actual are recomputed.
Failure_Behaviour: A rejected or coerced value can never be left on screen as if it had saved.
Evidence_Quote: "The value comes from the SERVER's response, never from the typed string, so a rejected or coerced value can never be left on screen as if it had saved."

Rule_Statement: The Vendor filter offers only vendors actually named on a line of THIS BOQ, in first-appearance order.
Failure_Behaviour: No error; a vendor not on the BOQ simply cannot be chosen.
Evidence_Quote: "Offering the org's whole supplier list would let a QS pick a vendor that empties the table."

Rule_Statement: Budget totals SKIP nulls rather than counting them as zero: an unquoted line must not drag the vendor total down.
Failure_Behaviour: Total returns null when every contributing value is null.
Evidence_Quote: "Nulls are SKIPPED, not counted as zero -- an unquoted line must not drag the vendor total down"

Rule_Statement: Export is DISABLED when the rows on screen do not sum to the total printed under them (tolerance one currency unit, 0.01).
Failure_Behaviour: Export blocked with the sentence "Totals do not tie: the lines add up to X but the total says Y".
Evidence_Quote: "the rows on screen must sum to the total printed under them, or Export is disabled WITH this sentence as its reason. A wrong file outlives a wrong screen."

Rule_Statement: Browser-built CSV exports prefix any value starting with = + - or @ with an apostrophe (formula-injection guard), because BOQ descriptions, categories and vendor names are user-typed free text.
Failure_Behaviour: Value is escaped; no error shown.

Rule_Statement: In the variance chart, a row with nothing costed yet (variance null) is LEFT OUT rather than drawn at zero, and bars are sorted worst-first (ascending on budget-remaining).
Failure_Behaviour: Row omitted from the chart.
Evidence_Quote: "A row with nothing costed yet carries variance null and is LEFT OUT rather than drawn at zero -- a bar at the origin reads as \"on budget\", which is a claim nobody made."

Rule_Statement: A daily progress entry requires Activity, Date, Quantity done, % complete and Entry basis; a BOQ line is ALSO required when the project has at least one BOQ, and is not required when it has none.
Failure_Behaviour: Log Entry button disabled and names the missing field; the server independently raises BOQ_LINE_REQUIRED.
Evidence_Quote: "the project has at least one BOQ -> a BOQ line is required / the project has no BOQ -> there is nothing to link to"

Rule_Statement: Business-rule refusals from the construction data service are returned as CODES plus the missing field, never as backend prose; the user-facing sentence is chosen from a closed client-side vocabulary.
Failure_Behaviour: Response body is {code, missing} at the upstream status; the browser renders the mapped sentence.
Evidence_Quote: "if (err instanceof VeridianApiError && err.ruleCode) { return NextResponse.json({ code: err.ruleCode, missing: err.missing ?? [] }, { status: err.status }); }"

Rule_Statement: Progress goes on a CHILD BOQ line, never a parent line.
Failure_Behaviour: Server returns BOQ_LINE_IS_PARENT; the screen shows "<code> is a parent line -- pick one of its child lines" with a Pick line action.
Evidence_Quote: "return code ? `${code} is a parent line -- pick one of its child lines` : \"Progress goes on a child line, not the parent\";"

Rule_Statement: A percent-complete value must be between 0 and 100.
Failure_Behaviour: Server returns VALUE_OUT_OF_RANGE; the screen shows "Type a number between 0 and 100" with a Type value action.
Evidence_Quote: "VALUE_OUT_OF_RANGE: { message: () => \"Type a number between 0 and 100\", ...pick(\"Type value\", \"value\", \"value\") },"

Rule_Statement: A BOQ line referenced by an entry must exist on that project's BOQ (and named version); otherwise the entry is refused.
Failure_Behaviour: BOQ_LINE_NOT_FOUND, rendered as "There is no line <code> on <project/version> -- pick a line".
Evidence_Quote: "if (code && where) return `There is no line ${code} on ${where} -- pick a line`;"

Rule_Statement: Recording is refused when the user's role does not permit it; classification/preview never authorizes execution.
Failure_Behaviour: NOT_PERMITTED, rendered as "Your role does not allow that".
Evidence_Quote: "NOT_PERMITTED: { message: () => \"Your role does not allow that\", ...openRoute(\"Open Home\", \"/dashboard\") },"

Rule_Statement: A SNAPSHOT-basis entry REPLACES rather than adds: the latest cumulative reading up to the report end date is authoritative, and qty/amt are derived from that percentage rather than from the row's own quantityDone.
Failure_Behaviour: No error; the report's qty, amt and percentage stay mutually consistent by construction.
Evidence_Quote: "a SNAPSHOT entry (30% then 60%, both rows kept in history ... ) reports whatever the LATEST reading says, replacing rather than adding"

Rule_Statement: A BOQ line that HAS children has its own directly-recorded progress REPLACED by a weighted roll-up of its children (cum qty = SUM(child cum qty x child breakdown% / 100)); the weighting is applied exactly once. A parent with no children is unchanged.
Failure_Behaviour: No error. KNOWN LIMITATION: only one level of nesting rolls up correctly.
Evidence_Quote: "cum qty = SUM(child cum qty * child breakdownPercentage / 100)"

Rule_Statement: Progress entries inside the report window that no BOQ line can claim are NOT counted in the report, and the count of them is stated above the table.
Failure_Behaviour: Note shown: "N entries not linked to a BOQ line are not counted"; null (silent) when the count is zero.
Evidence_Quote: "if (count === 1) return \"1 entry not linked to a BOQ line is not counted\";"

Rule_Statement: Percentage cells are for PARENT rows only; a hierarchical child's percentage cell always renders blank, never a number. A parent always renders a real number, 0% included.
Failure_Behaviour: Blank cell for children; "0%" for an untouched parent.
Evidence_Quote: "a parent line always renders a real number (0% included); only a child's cell is ever blank."

Rule_Statement: A never-touched bucket renders blank; a real computed zero renders "-". The two are different facts and must not look alike.
Failure_Behaviour: No error; purely a rendering rule shared by the tab, the PDF and the public share page.
Evidence_Quote: "if (!touched) return \"\"; if (value === 0) return \"-\"; return value;"

Rule_Statement: The report's Grand Total sums ROOT (non-child) lines' contract amounts only, the same "parent BOQ lines only" rule the PDF and share page use.
Failure_Behaviour: No error; prevents double counting.
Evidence_Quote: "Grand Total sums root (non-child) lines' own amtTotal only"

Rule_Statement: Balance = the line's own BOQ total minus (previous + current) progress. Both Total and Balance are shown; the user chooses.
Failure_Behaviour: Derived, nothing new is persisted.
Evidence_Quote: "balance = original (this line's own BoQ total) - total (previous + current). Both are legitimate readings of the same three stored numbers -- nothing new is persisted."

Rule_Statement: A row's Category is resolved in strict order: the line's own category, then its parent's category, then its activity's category, then the parent's item code, and only then "Uncategorized".
Failure_Behaviour: No error; "Uncategorized" only for a root line with no category and no activity.
Evidence_Quote: "realCategory(line.category) ?? realCategory(parentLine?.category) ?? realCategory(activityCategoryName) ?? realCategory(parentLine?.itemCode) ?? UNCATEGORIZED_LABEL"

Rule_Statement: Deleting a progress entry must state its blast radius before the click: quantity, unit, date, the target line, and the running total before and after. Percentages are omitted (not shown as 0%) when the line has no contracted amount.
Failure_Behaviour: Confirmation sentence; without a denominator it ends at "This cannot be undone." rather than printing "0% to 0%".
Evidence_Quote: "the running total drops from ${impact.percentBefore}% to ${impact.percentAfter}%."

Rule_Statement: The report's category filter is case-insensitive, and an empty or all-blank filter means EVERY category, never none.
Failure_Behaviour: Applied server-side before the rollup so subtotals and Grand Total describe the filtered set.
Evidence_Quote: "An empty or all-blank filter means every category, never none: returning an empty report there would look exactly like \"this project has no BOQ\""

Rule_Statement: The Work Progress Report runs on arrival with from/to/view/boqVersion taken from the URL; anything absent or unusable falls back to first-of-current-month through today rather than blocking the run.
Failure_Behaviour: Bad bookmark still shows the current month.
Evidence_Quote: "Anything absent or unusable falls back to the default rather than blocking the run"

Rule_Statement: The report views are limited to scope, category, manpower and vendor; an unrecognised view falls back to "scope".
Failure_Behaviour: Silent fallback.
Evidence_Quote: "export const WPR_VIEWS = [\"scope\", \"category\", \"manpower\", \"vendor\"] as const;"

Rule_Statement: boqVersion in the report URL must be a positive integer; otherwise the server picks the latest live BOQ version.
Failure_Behaviour: Silent fallback to null.
Evidence_Quote: "return Number.isInteger(n) && n > 0 ? n : null;"

Rule_Statement: Logged % (site-recorded average per activity) and Earned % (BOQ value delivered) are DIFFERENT measures. The explanatory note is shown only in the one fixable disagreement: logged progress exists but every category has earned 0%.
Failure_Behaviour: Note rendered under the tags; suppressed while the report has not answered.
Evidence_Quote: "Logged progress is not yet linked to BOQ lines, so earned value is 0% - link entries to BOQ lines when recording progress."

Rule_Statement: The report's default date window comes from the DATA (earliest entry through today), not from today's month alone.
Failure_Behaviour: A project whose entries are all older still reports on a window that shows them.
Evidence_Quote: "Defaults come from the DATA, not from today's date: the earliest entry the project has, through today."

Rule_Statement: Every Work Progress export is named <project>-work-progress-<from>-<to>.<ext>, ASCII-slugged, matching the server's own Content-Disposition rule.
Failure_Behaviour: Server header wins for PDF/XLSX; the browser-built CSV uses the identical rule.
Evidence_Quote: "return `${slug || \"project\"}-work-progress-${from}-${to}.${extension}`;"

Rule_Statement: Correcting or deleting one progress entry runs exactly the same validation as recording it, and the backend's rule message is passed through verbatim.
Failure_Behaviour: Upstream status and message returned; an unparseable body is a 400 "A JSON body is required".
Evidence_Quote: "it runs exactly the same validation the create path runs. The backend's message is passed through verbatim rather than replaced with a generic one"

Rule_Statement: The daily attendance draft stores the EXCEPTIONS (who is absent / half day), not who is present, so a worker added to the roster after the sheet opened defaults to present.
Failure_Behaviour: No error; the state survives a reload of the roster it describes.
Evidence_Quote: "Storing \"who is NOT present\" means a new name is present by default, which is the truth on most days"

Rule_Statement: Marking a worker absent clears any half-day mark on them, and a half day can never be applied to somebody marked absent.
Failure_Behaviour: toggleHalfDay returns the draft unchanged for an absent worker.
Evidence_Quote: "a half day for someone who was not there is not a state the payroll should ever be handed."

Rule_Statement: Attendance cost multipliers are: present = 1, half day = 0.5, absent = 0. Row cost = daily rate x multiplier, rounded to 2dp. The SERVER recomputes every cost from the roster's own dailyRate on save and is authoritative.
Failure_Behaviour: The saved total is taken from the server's response, not from the client figure.
Evidence_Quote: "const COST_MULTIPLIER: Record<AttendanceStatus, number> = { present: 1, half_day: 0.5, absent: 0 };"

Rule_Statement: An UNMARKED row is not the same as Absent: it contributes to no subtotal, no count and no cost, and renders as an em dash.
Failure_Behaviour: Row skipped in summariseByTrade; rowCost returns null.
Evidence_Quote: "computed over MARKED rows only -- an unmarked worker contributes to nothing, which is the whole reason unmarked and Absent must look different on screen."

Rule_Statement: Headcount "on site" = present + half day. An absence is not a body on site.
Failure_Behaviour: A window with nobody says so in words rather than showing a bare 0.
Evidence_Quote: "Bodies on site means present plus half day; an absence is not a body."

Rule_Statement: A worker with no trade recorded is grouped under "Unspecified", sorted last, and is never dropped or shown under a blank heading.
Failure_Behaviour: Group always present when such rows exist.
Evidence_Quote: "export const UNSPECIFIED_TRADE = \"Unspecified\";"

Rule_Statement: Saving attendance a second time for the same date REPLACES what is saved; the confirmation must name the number of rows overwritten before the user agrees.
Failure_Behaviour: Warning sentence: "Attendance for <day> is already saved -- replace it? This overwrites what is saved and writes N rows."
Evidence_Quote: "a replace deletes rows that are already someone's payroll input, and the number of them is the fact that decides whether the answer is yes."

Rule_Statement: Attendance for a given worker on a given date cannot be recorded twice through the composer path.
Failure_Behaviour: ALREADY_RECORDED, rendered as "Attendance is already recorded for that worker on that date".
Evidence_Quote: "if (fn === \"record_attendance\") return \"Attendance is already recorded for that worker on that date\";"

Rule_Statement: Export of the attendance summary is BLOCKED when the per-trade rows do not add up to the window totals.
Failure_Behaviour: Banner shown and Export disabled with reason "Rows do not sum to the totals".
Evidence_Quote: "The per-trade rows do not add up to the totals for this window. Export is disabled until this is resolved."

Rule_Statement: "This week" on the attendance panel runs Monday to Sunday (ISO), anchored on the chosen date; "This month" is the calendar month of that date.
Failure_Behaviour: No error; matches the weekly project report's own week.
Evidence_Quote: "\"This week\" runs Monday to Sunday. That is a choice, not a universal: it matches the ISO week this codebase already uses for weeklyProjectReport's weekStart"

Rule_Statement: The attendance read is dated: one day by default (the reader's LOCAL calendar day), or a 7-day inclusive window ending on that day when "Show earlier days" is used. Never the project's whole undated log.
Failure_Behaviour: Query built as ?date= or ?from=&?to=.
Evidence_Quote: "export const EARLIER_DAYS = 7;"

Rule_Statement: "Today" for attendance is the reader's local calendar day, not UTC, because attendance_date is a plain date column with no timezone.
Failure_Behaviour: Prevents a foreman in UTC+4 being shown yesterday's rows before 04:00.
Evidence_Quote: "at 01:00 in Dubai (UTC+4) that returns YESTERDAY, so a foreman marking the morning's attendance would be shown the previous day's rows"

Rule_Statement: The whole roster for one date is saved in ONE call inside a single upstream transaction, and answers 200 rather than 201 because re-saving corrects rows that already exist.
Failure_Behaviour: On failure the upstream status and message are returned; nothing partial is written.
Evidence_Quote: "200, not 201: re-saving a sheet corrects rows that already exist, so this is not always a creation."

Rule_Statement: Attendance save failures speak a fixed vocabulary by status and always state whether anything was saved: 400 check the marked rows, 403 no permission, 404 worker no longer on the roster, 409 sheet changed while marking.
Failure_Behaviour: Sentence + Retry; raw backend strings (which carry row ids) are never printed.
Evidence_Quote: "if (status === 409) return \"This sheet changed while you were marking it -- reload the sheet. Nothing was saved.\";"

Rule_Statement: A new activity requires a Title and a Start date.
Failure_Behaviour: Save disabled: a count while more than one is missing, the field NAME once only one is left.
Evidence_Quote: "export function missingActivityFields(draft: ActivityDraft): string[]"

Rule_Statement: An activity's Due date must be on or after its Start date.
Failure_Behaviour: Blur message "Due date is before the start date -- pick a later date"; no message while either date is empty.
Evidence_Quote: "export const DUE_BEFORE_START_MESSAGE = \"Due date is before the start date -- pick a later date\";"

Rule_Statement: Activity duration is the literal difference due minus start (NOT difference + 1). An activity that starts and finishes on the same day has duration 0, and that zero-length window IS what a milestone means.
Failure_Behaviour: Unset dates render the en dash rather than a number.
Evidence_Quote: "Deliberately the literal difference, not difference+1 -- an activity that starts and finishes on the same day has a duration of 0 days here, which is what a milestone is"

Rule_Statement: Typing a duration moves the finish date and typing a finish date moves the duration. A negative or non-numeric duration derives nothing and the field is left alone rather than cleared.
Failure_Behaviour: Returns null; the user's typed date is not overwritten.
Evidence_Quote: "if (!Number.isFinite(days) || days < 0) return null;"

Rule_Statement: Slip = actual due date minus BASELINE planned due date; positive means late. Null (en dash) when the activity has no baseline snapshot or either date is missing -- never 0.
Failure_Behaviour: Renders "+3 d late" / "2 d early" / "0 d on time" / en dash, always with the word, never colour or glyph alone.
Evidence_Quote: "Null when this activity has no baseline snapshot, or either side has no due date -- which is a different fact from \"on time\" and must not collapse into 0."

Rule_Statement: Planned % complete = clamp((today - planned start) / (planned due - planned start)) as a percentage. A zero-length or inverted window is either wholly due or wholly not, never a division.
Failure_Behaviour: Returns null when any date is missing or unparseable.
Evidence_Quote: "if (due <= start) return now >= due ? 100 : 0;"

Rule_Statement: Slippage in days = ((planned% - actual%) / 100) x duration, priced in that activity's own calendar. Any missing input yields null ("we cannot say"), never 0.
Failure_Behaviour: Renders the en dash; a rose glyph is used only for "behind", and always with the word.
Evidence_Quote: "Every input that is missing yields `null` -- \"we cannot say\" -- and never 0, which would read as \"on track\"."

Rule_Statement: The programme tile reports the WORST single activity's slip, not an average.
Failure_Behaviour: "Schedule: N tasks behind, worst M days", or a sentence saying no activity has both dates yet.
Evidence_Quote: "worstSlipDays is the WORST activity, not an average: an average slip is a number no site meeting has ever asked for"

Rule_Statement: The New Task Type control is only openable when its options have loaded; a loading control shows NO text in the value slot. An empty or failed type list does NOT block Save, because the server applies the org's default type.
Failure_Behaviour: Control disabled with a stated hint; Save still permitted.
Evidence_Quote: "Task types come from VERIDIAN. Saving now uses your organisation's default type."

Rule_Statement: Manually overriding an activity's completion percentage REQUIRES a note, enforced server-side, and goes through its own endpoint separate from the ordinary task PATCH.
Failure_Behaviour: Upstream refusal surfaced verbatim: "A note is required when you set the percentage manually".
Evidence_Quote: "the override REQUIRES a note, enforced server-side, and collapsing them here would put the one endpoint that enforces that rule behind one that does not."

Rule_Statement: Never render a currency token that cannot be sourced. Order: the org's base-currency row, then NEXT_PUBLIC_DEFAULT_CURRENCY_CODE, then the bare number with no currency token at all.
Failure_Behaviour: An unlabelled amount rather than a confidently wrong symbol.
Evidence_Quote: "An unlabelled \"1,000\" is recoverable -- the reader knows something is missing. A confidently wrong \"₹1,000\" is not: it reads as fact."

Rule_Statement: Setting the organisation's base currency requires a 3-letter ISO code and is owner/admin only; reading it is open to any authenticated member.
Failure_Behaviour: 400 'code must be a 3-letter ISO currency code, e.g. "AED"'; 403 for a non-admin.
Evidence_Quote: "if (!/^[A-Z]{3}$/.test(code)) { return NextResponse.json({ error: 'code must be a 3-letter ISO currency code, e.g. \"AED\"' }, { status: 400 }); }"

Rule_Statement: The cached org currency list is cleared on sign-out, so a second sign-in in the same tab cannot read the previous org's codes.
Failure_Behaviour: Cache cleared; next read refetches.
Evidence_Quote: "without it a second sign-in in the same tab could read the previous org's codes until the refetch landed."

Rule_Statement: Across money and count cells, a null figure renders as an en dash and a real zero renders as "0" / "0.00" -- "we do not know" and "it is zero" are never shown identically.
Failure_Behaviour: Display rule shared by the panel, the CSV and the public share page.
Evidence_Quote: "\"0\" for a real measured zero, \"-\" for no figure at all. These are different facts ... and a table that renders them identically is lying about one of them."

Rule_Statement: A create screen's primary button is DISABLED until every required field is filled, and it NAMES what is missing rather than failing after the click.
Failure_Behaviour: Save disabled with "Save (Title, Line 1)"-shaped reason.
Evidence_Quote: "instead of an enabled Save on an empty form that fails only after the click."

Rule_Statement: A checkbox field is never marked required -- an unticked box is an answer, so "required checkbox" has no honest meaning.
Failure_Behaviour: Convention enforced by the field-kind contract.
Evidence_Quote: "Never mark one `required` -- an unticked box is an answer, so \"required checkbox\" has no honest meaning."

Rule_Statement: A form whose precondition is not met must disable its inputs WITH a stated reason; disabled in silence is a defect, and live inputs on a form that cannot accept them is a defect.
Failure_Behaviour: Control disabled and the reason shown on the control itself.
Evidence_Quote: "Disabled WITH a reason is the product's rule; disabled in silence is the defect."

Rule_Statement: After a successful create the app goes to the new object's page in display mode with "Created <object> <identifier>", never back to an empty form or a list.
Failure_Behaviour: Footer receipt message; falls back to the record id only when there is no recognisable identifier.
Evidence_Quote: "never back to an empty form or a list."

Rule_Statement: Delete confirmations name the blast radius and end "This cannot be undone." rather than asking "are you sure".
Failure_Behaviour: Confirmation sentence naming the record and what goes with it.
Evidence_Quote: "return `Delete ${subject}${tail}? This cannot be undone.`;"

Rule_Statement: A roster worker requires a Name and a Daily Rate that is a real, non-negative number; "abc" and "-5" are both refused.
Failure_Behaviour: Save disabled naming "Name, Daily Rate"; the server's own dailyRate guard refuses both too.
Evidence_Quote: "A rate is usable when it is a real, non-negative number. \"abc\" and \"-5\" are NOT usable: the server refuses both"

Rule_Statement: Logged hours must be greater than 0, at most 24, and in steps of 0.25. Task, Date and Category are required.
Failure_Behaviour: Field message "Enter hours greater than 0, in steps of 0.25 (max 24)"; an empty field is treated as not-yet-filled, not invalid.
Evidence_Quote: "export const HOURS_STEP = 0.25; export const HOURS_MAX = 24;"

Rule_Statement: A permit requires a name, issue date, end date and a PDF; the end date must be on or after the issue date; the file must be a .pdf of at most 10 MB.
Failure_Behaviour: Save disabled with "N required fields still needed - ..."; file errors state both the file's size and the limit.
Evidence_Quote: "export const MAX_PDF_MB = 10;" / "return endDate < issueDate ? \"End date must be on or after the issue date\" : undefined;"

Rule_Statement: An uploaded document may be at most 25 MB, and its category must be one of permit, drawing, contract, certificate, license, site_photo, email, other.
Failure_Behaviour: Message "This file is 31 MB; the limit is 25 MB" before the upload rather than after it.
Evidence_Quote: "export const DOCUMENT_MAX_MB = 25;"

Rule_Statement: A DWG drawing file must be .dwg, .dxf or .pdf; a 3D walkthrough file must be .glb, .gltf, .fbx or .mp4. The picker filter is not treated as a guarantee.
Failure_Behaviour: "Choose a .dwg, .dxf or .pdf file -- this is a .png".

Rule_Statement: A file's size is stated in the same unit as the limit, using one decimal only where whole-number rounding would read "This file is 10 MB; the limit is 10 MB".
Failure_Behaviour: Message shown at the field before upload.
Evidence_Quote: "a 10.4 MB file refused by a 10 MB limit must not read \"10 MB\"."

Rule_Statement: The organisation role axis has exactly six values: owner, admin, pm, site_engineer, member, client_viewer. It is not a linear rank -- client_viewer and site_engineer restrict along different axes.
Failure_Behaviour: A role outside the set is refused by the DB check constraint on memberships.role and by API validation.
Evidence_Quote: "check (role in ('owner', 'admin', 'pm', 'site_engineer', 'member', 'client_viewer'));" (drizzle/0012_membership_roles_pm_site_engineer.sql)

Rule_Statement: EVERY mutating /api request (POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE) is role-gated at one middleware choke point against one checked-in policy table. GET is deliberately NOT role-gated.
Failure_Behaviour: 403 {"error":"Forbidden: your role does not permit this action"}.
Evidence_Quote: "export const MUTATING_METHODS: ReadonlySet<string> = new Set([\"POST\", \"PUT\", \"PATCH\", \"DELETE\"]);"

Rule_Statement: A route with no entry in the write-policy table does not inherit the weakest tier: it falls back to FIELD, and a missing entry fails the build test.
Failure_Behaviour: Unmatched paths resolve to the nearest ancestor pattern, then to FIELD -- never to "allow".
Evidence_Quote: "A route added without a policy entry must NOT quietly inherit the weakest tier ... it lands on the same tier as on-site work rather than on \"anyone\"."

Rule_Statement: Financial, contractual, commercial and programme authority (budgets, change orders, purchase orders, invoices, quotations, projects, vendors, BOQ scope, baselines, schedule import) is owner/admin/pm only -- site_engineer and client_viewer are excluded.
Failure_Behaviour: 403 for site_engineer, member and client_viewer.
Evidence_Quote: "PM_OR_ABOVE: [\"owner\", \"admin\", \"pm\"] as const," -- "Financial / contractual / commercial / schedule authority ... Deliberately excludes site_engineer and client_viewer."

Rule_Statement: Work actually recorded on site (attendance, work progress, punch list, site diary, materials, documents, drawings, RFIs, submittals, schedule tasks) is owner/admin/pm/site_engineer -- the legacy `member` role and client_viewer are excluded.
Failure_Behaviour: 403 for member and client_viewer.
Evidence_Quote: "FIELD: [\"owner\", \"admin\", \"pm\", \"site_engineer\"] as const,"

Rule_Statement: Org membership, security/compliance posture, HR and payroll master data, recruitment hiring and the general ledger are owner/admin only.
Failure_Behaviour: 403 for pm, site_engineer, member, client_viewer.
Evidence_Quote: "ORG_ADMIN: [\"owner\", \"admin\"] as const," -- "Hiring creates an employee record and a payroll liability."

Rule_Statement: Self-service on one's OWN record (filing own leave, logging/submitting own time, own to-dos) is open to every role except client_viewer; DECIDING someone else's (approve/reject leave or timesheets) is PM or above.
Failure_Behaviour: 403 on the decision routes for a non-PM.
Evidence_Quote: "Filing your OWN leave request is self-service; DECIDING one is not."

Rule_Statement: Minting a public, unauthenticated share link (report, attendance summary, minutes) is PM or above, not field level, because handing the org's cost figures outside the org is a manager's decision.
Failure_Behaviour: 403 for site_engineer on the /share routes.
Evidence_Quote: "deliberately NOT \"FIELD\", because handing the org's cost figures outside the org is a manager's decision."

Rule_Statement: Actions every authenticated member may take regardless of role, client_viewer included: marking a notification read, replying in a conversation, accepting an invite addressed to them, recording their own composer pill usage.
Failure_Behaviour: Allowed for all six roles.
Evidence_Quote: "Accepting an invite addressed to you is how you GET a role -- gating it on one would be circular."

Rule_Statement: Overruling an activity's completion percentage is a PM judgement (PM_OR_ABOVE), while recording site progress through /work-progress stays FIELD.
Failure_Behaviour: 403 for a site_engineer calling the completion override.
Evidence_Quote: "overruling a completion percentage derived from the site's own records is a PM judgement, not a field entry"

Rule_Statement: A role gate hidden only in the UI is not a control: the boundary is server-side. Composer classification/preview executes nothing and never authorizes -- what a user may RUN is re-checked at execution.
Failure_Behaviour: Preview always returns executed:false; execution is gated separately.
Evidence_Quote: "THIS IS A SERVER-SIDE GATE, NOT A UI ONE ... hiding a button is a UX affordance and never the boundary."

Rule_Statement: Page access is deny-by-default: every page is authenticated unless it is on the explicit public list (/, /hi, /how-it-works, /login, /signup) or under /auth/, /invite/, /share/, /shared/.
Failure_Behaviour: Unauthenticated visitor is redirected to /login with ?redirectTo=<path>.
Evidence_Quote: "an allow-list of protected paths fails open ... A deny-list of PUBLIC paths fails closed"

Rule_Statement: /api/* is excluded from the page gate, so an API 401 stays JSON and never becomes a 307 redirect to an HTML login page.
Failure_Behaviour: API routes return their own 401 JSON.
Evidence_Quote: "THE CLAUSE THAT MUST NOT BE DROPPED: /api/* is excluded here."

Rule_Statement: An already-authenticated visitor who opens the marketing landing route is sent to /dashboard.
Failure_Behaviour: 307 redirect to /dashboard.
Evidence_Quote: "if (userId && isLandingRoute(pathname)) { const url = request.nextUrl.clone(); url.pathname = \"/dashboard\";"

Rule_Statement: If the membership lookup fails while checking a write, the request is REFUSED rather than guessed -- a transient lookup failure is neither "no organization" nor a role refusal.
Failure_Behaviour: 503 {"error":"Could not verify organization membership, please retry"}.
Evidence_Quote: "Fail closed on the write, but say why."

Rule_Statement: Every PROJEXA->VERIDIAN call authenticates with one ORG-scoped API key; no user id or role crosses that boundary, so per-user role gating is structurally only possible on the PROJEXA side.
Failure_Behaviour: A missing per-org credential row throws a fail-loud configuration error rather than silently using a fallback key.
Evidence_Quote: "No user id and no role crosses that boundary, so VERIDIAN is structurally incapable of a per-user role refusal on these calls."

Rule_Statement: An authenticated user with no resolved membership is a 400 "No organization", not a 403; an unauthenticated caller is a 401.
Failure_Behaviour: 400 / 401 / 503 as appropriate; the write-policy check returns "allowed" for a null role so the route can produce the accurate status.
Evidence_Quote: "return { user, organizationId: null, role: null, response: NextResponse.json({ error: \"No organization\" }, { status: 400 }) };"

Rule_Statement: Changing a member's role is owner/admin only and the new role must be one of the six valid roles.
Failure_Behaviour: 403 for a non-admin; 400 "role must be one of: ..." for an invalid role; 404 when the member is not in this org.
Evidence_Quote: "if (!role || !ALL_ORG_ROLES.includes(role as OrgRole)) { return NextResponse.json({ error: `role must be one of: ${ALL_ORG_ROLES.join(\", \")}` }, { status: 400 }); }"

Rule_Statement: An organisation must always keep at least one owner or admin: demoting the last one is refused, including self-demotion.
Failure_Behaviour: 409 "Cannot change this member's role: every organization must keep at least one owner or admin."
Evidence_Quote: "every organization must keep at least one owner or admin."

Rule_Statement: An invitation requires a syntactically valid email address and a valid role (default 'member'); the error names the field and the reason.
Failure_Behaviour: 400 with the specific field named, e.g. 'Email "x" is not a valid email address.'
Evidence_Quote: "UAT criterion C04 (INPUT_REJECTED) requires the message to name the field and the reason, not a generic \"invalid request\"."

Rule_Statement: Somebody who is already a member of the organisation cannot be invited again.
Failure_Behaviour: 409 "<email> is already a member of this organisation."
Evidence_Quote: "Inviting somebody who is already in this organisation would otherwise look like it worked and then never appear anywhere."

Rule_Statement: At most ONE live (unaccepted, unrevoked) invite may exist per organisation + email; a re-invite must revoke or consume the old one first.
Failure_Behaviour: Partial unique index violation (23505) surfaced as 409 "There is already a pending invitation for <email>. Revoke it first to issue a new link."
Evidence_Quote: "create unique index if not exists org_invites_one_pending_per_email on public.org_invites (organization_id, lower(email)) where accepted_at is null and revoked_at is null;"

Rule_Statement: An invitation expires 14 days after it is created.
Failure_Behaviour: Redemption raises "This invitation has expired. Ask an administrator for a new one."
Evidence_Quote: "expires_at timestamptz not null default (now() + interval '14 days'),"

Rule_Statement: An invite is BOUND to its email address: a token redeemed by a user whose profile email differs is refused, so a leaked link grants nothing.
Failure_Behaviour: Exception "This invitation was issued to a different email address." (surfaced verbatim as a 400).
Evidence_Quote: "if v_email is null or lower(v_email) <> lower(v_invite.email) then raise exception 'This invitation was issued to a different email address.'"

Rule_Statement: A revoked invitation, and an invitation that has already been used, cannot be redeemed.
Failure_Behaviour: Exceptions "This invitation has been revoked." / "This invitation has already been used."
Evidence_Quote: "if v_invite.revoked_at is not null then raise exception 'This invitation has been revoked.'"

Rule_Statement: Accepting an invite is idempotent on membership (an existing membership row is left alone) and always writes a security audit log row naming the org and role granted.
Failure_Behaviour: No duplicate membership; audit row 'org_invite.accepted' inserted.
Evidence_Quote: "insert into public.memberships (user_id, organization_id, role) values (v_uid, v_invite.organization_id, v_invite.role) on conflict (user_id, organization_id) do nothing;"

Rule_Statement: An invitee may see who invited them and to what (org name, role, expiry, whether the link is still open) WITHOUT the token, the email or anything else in the invite row being exposed.
Failure_Behaviour: Security-definer view function returns org name + role only.
Evidence_Quote: "Returns org name + role only."

Rule_Statement: Reading, creating and revoking invites through an ordinary session is limited to org owners/admins by row-level security, mirroring the application role group.
Failure_Behaviour: RLS policy blocks the row entirely for non-admins.
Evidence_Quote: "create policy \"org admins can create invites in their organization\" on public.org_invites for insert with check ( ... m.role in ('owner', 'admin') )"

Rule_Statement: Redemption is deliberately not behind the normal org guard, because the redeeming user is by definition not yet a member of any organisation.
Failure_Behaviour: 401 if not signed in; otherwise every authorisation decision is delegated to the database function.
Evidence_Quote: "Deliberately NOT behind requireAuth(): requireAuth() answers 400 \"No organization\" for exactly the user this route exists to serve"

Rule_Statement: A failure message never prints a backend identifier: no IP:port, host:port, ECONN*/CONNECT_TIMEOUT, camelCase parameter name or function id ever reaches a screen; a masked string reads "service unavailable".
Failure_Behaviour: The sentence is chosen by CODE, never copied from the backend's text; a masking pass is the last line of defence.
Evidence_Quote: "never a camelCase parameter name, never a function id, never a host, an address or a port."

Rule_Statement: Every blocked action carries a VERB button -- "Pick line", "Choose project", "Type value", "Retry" -- so a refused row always has a way out and never a dead end.
Failure_Behaviour: Button rendered beside the sentence; an "open" action renders no button when no real destination exists.
Evidence_Quote: "Every pickable failure carries a VERB LABEL for its button ... so a blocked row always has a way out and never a dead end."

Rule_Statement: Retry is offered ONLY for transport failures, where nothing was written and repeating is safe. A 4xx refusal is never a Retry, and a "fix" action loads the picker and STOPS -- it must never re-execute.
Failure_Behaviour: RECORD_NOT_FOUND, ALREADY_RECORDED and REQUEST_REJECTED offer a route, not a retry.
Evidence_Quote: "None of these three is a Retry: sending the same request again cannot change a 4xx."

Rule_Statement: Every failure sentence states whether anything was saved ("nothing was saved").
Failure_Behaviour: Sentence includes the clause; the composer and the Daily Entry form print the same words for the same failure.
Evidence_Quote: "BACKEND_UNAVAILABLE: { message: () => \"The construction data service didn't answer -- nothing was saved\", ...RETRY_STEP },"

Rule_Statement: A BOQ that has already been revised cannot be revised a second time; the user is sent to the latest revision.
Failure_Behaviour: ALREADY_RECORDED with functionId create_boq_revision -> "That BOQ has already been revised -- open the latest revision".
Evidence_Quote: "if (fn === \"create_boq_revision\") return \"That BOQ has already been revised -- open the latest revision\";"

Rule_Statement: A request that reads as a QUESTION rather than an instruction saves nothing.
Failure_Behaviour: READ_AS_QUESTION -> "That reads as a question, so nothing was saved".
Evidence_Quote: "READ_AS_QUESTION: { message: () => \"That reads as a question, so nothing was saved\", ...openRoute(\"Open Home\", \"/dashboard\") },"

Rule_Statement: A user cannot act on a project they do not have access to.
Failure_Behaviour: PROJECT_NOT_REACHABLE -> "You do not have access to that project -- pick another".
Evidence_Quote: "PROJECT_NOT_REACHABLE: { message: () => \"You do not have access to that project -- pick another\""
